newsitem.title: UK: UK says airlines backed London BAA formula.
newsitem.headline: UK says airlines backed London BAA formula.

text.p: Airlines which pay large portions of the charges at London's three main airports backed a new British formula for capping charges because they want to see new capacity at crowded Heathrow, the regulator said on Thursday.

In a statement explaining its decision to require airports operator BAA Plc to hold annual rises in its airline user charges at the large Heathrow and Gatwick airports at three percentage points below inflation for five years, the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) said airlines backed its plan.

"The airlines which pay the most in charges endorsed the proposals for RPI-3 on the basis that BAA should be encouraged to proceed with its large capital investment programme, including Terminal 5 at Heathrow," the CAA said.
However, it added they also sought assurances that the investments would be carried out "on time, to the standards they require and in close consultation with them".
"The airlines also felt that the RPI-3 formula would avoid the need for large and possibly unachievable increases after 2002, once Terminal 5 is opened," the CAA added.
The underlying issue throughout the preparations of this new price formula has been how to "smooth" the impact of a multi-billion stg invesment plan on charges now and beyond 2002.

Inherent in this five-year regulatory plan is a link through to the next five years because by avoiding "penal" capping in the run-up to Terminal 5, BAA is in effect being tied in to providing a soft landing for its customers once it is built. According to the CAA, its new formula implies that BAA "will be able to earn substantially more over the next five years than would have been possible if it had been set on the basis of the 1997-2002 period alone.
And, in case BAA had missed the point, it states "Should Terminal 5 not fo ahead, the formula will be reviewed before the end of the five-year period."
